notes: FIFO-related observations and influences use the specified black-box assumption for the external neorv32_fifo instances.

points.reached by: holding block
points.reason: An unchecked bus write changes ctrl.enable, and clearing it gates clock generation and clears both FIFOs.

points.reached by: the bus_access ==> tx_fifo.clear arrow carrying ctrl.enable
points.reason: This logic only forwards the enable-derived clear value to the FIFO and does not provide an independent observation or influence of the enable state.

points.reached by: the bus_access ==> rx_fifo.clear arrow carrying ctrl.enable
points.reason: This logic only forwards the enable-derived clear value to the FIFO and does not provide an independent observation or influence of the enable state.

points.reached by: the tx_fifo.clear ==> tx_fifo_inst arrow
points.reason: The FIFO is reached through the enable-derived clear input, but the black-box behavior gives no separate unauthorized observation or control of ctrl.enable at this point.

points.reached by: the rx_fifo.clear ==> rx_fifo_inst arrow
points.reason: The FIFO is reached through the enable-derived clear input, but the black-box behavior gives no separate unauthorized observation or control of ctrl.enable at this point.

points.reached by: the bus_access --> clock_generator arrow carrying ctrl.enable
points.reason: The clock generator uses ctrl.enable as a designed gate; this block does not independently modify or expose the stored enable state.

points.reached by: the bus_access ==> irq_generator arrow carrying ctrl.enable
points.reason: The interrupt expression uses ctrl.enable as a designed qualification and does not independently expose or modify the enable state.

points.reached by: the bus_access ==> transceiver arrow carrying ctrl.enable
points.reason: The transceiver uses ctrl.enable to select its state, but the block does not independently expose or modify the stored enable state.

points.reached by: held line
points.reason: This output directly reports ctrl.enable, but confidentiality is not an objective for this concept and the output cannot modify the stored state.

points.reached by: holding block
points.reason: Unchecked bus writes change the prescaler, divider, and high-speed fields, which select the clock-generation timing and can stall or make transfers unusable.

points.reached by: the bus_access --> clock_generator arrow carrying ctrl.cdiv, ctrl.enable, ctrl.highspeed and ctrl.prsc
points.reason: This block uses the stored settings as designed; it does not independently modify or expose the configuration.

points.reached by: the bus_req_i ==> tx_fifo.wdata arrow carrying bus_req_i.data
points.reason: The bus write data is present on the FIFO write-data path, so it can be observed there and an unchecked bus write can alter the transmitted payload.

points.reached by: the bus_req_i --> tx_fifo.we arrow
points.reason: The unchecked strobe, direction, and address conditions decide whether a transmit payload is accepted, allowing injection or suppression of queued data.

points.reached by: backward from tx_fifo_inst through the tx_fifo.clear ==> tx_fifo_inst arrow
points.reason: The enable-derived clear input can clear queued transmit data before it is sent.

points.reached by: the tx_fifo.wdata ==> tx_fifo_inst arrow
points.reason: Under the black-box rule, the FIFO input can be stored and returned on rdata, while its write, clear, and availability behavior can alter or block the payload transfer.

points.reached by: the tx_fifo_inst ==> transceiver arrow carrying tx_fifo.rdata
points.reason: The FIFO word is loaded into rtx_engine.sreg and later shifted to the serial output; FIFO availability and the clocked state machine can alter or prevent transmission.

points.reached by: held line
points.reason: spi_dat_o directly exposes the transmitted shift-register bit, so the payload is observable at the external serial-data boundary.

points.reached by: holding block
points.reason: spi_dat_i is sampled into the receive shift path, so its value can alter the received payload; the clocked state machine can also delay or prevent completion.

points.reached by: the transceiver ==> rx_fifo.wdata arrow carrying rtx_engine.sreg
points.reason: The reconstructed receive word is present on the FIFO write-data path and can be observed or altered before buffering.

points.reached by: the transceiver ==> rx_fifo.we arrow carrying rtx_engine.done
points.reason: The completion pulse decides whether the received word is written into the receive FIFO, so suppressing it can withhold the payload.

points.reached by: backward from rx_fifo_inst through the rx_fifo.clear ==> rx_fifo_inst arrow
points.reason: The enable-derived clear path can discard received data before it is returned to the bus.

points.reached by: backward from rx_fifo_inst through the rx_fifo.re ==> rx_fifo_inst arrow
points.reason: The bus-controlled read enable can pop or withhold the receive FIFO word and therefore affect its availability.

points.reached by: the rx_fifo.wdata ==> rx_fifo_inst arrow
points.reason: Under the black-box rule, the FIFO stores and returns the received word, while clear, write, and read behavior can alter or block its availability.

points.reached by: the rx_fifo_inst ==> bus_access arrow carrying rx_fifo.rdata
points.reason: The receive FIFO word is copied into the bus response, exposing the payload; bus-controlled reads and FIFO-pop behavior can withhold it.

points.reached by: the bus_req_i ==> tx_fifo.wdata arrow carrying bus_req_i.data
points.reason: The bus write supplies the chip-select command word, so an unchecked write can alter or prevent the queued target-selection command.

points.reached by: the bus_req_i --> tx_fifo.we arrow
points.reason: The bus strobe, direction, and address decide whether the target-selection command enters the FIFO.

points.reached by: backward from tx_fifo_inst through the tx_fifo.clear ==> tx_fifo_inst arrow
points.reason: The enable-derived clear can remove a queued chip-select command and leave the targets deselected.

points.reached by: the tx_fifo.wdata ==> tx_fifo_inst arrow
points.reason: Under the black-box rule, the FIFO can store, return, suppress, or clear the command that determines chip selection.

points.reached by: the tx_fifo_inst ==> transceiver arrow carrying tx_fifo.rdata
points.reason: The queued command loads rtx_engine.cs_ctrl, while FIFO availability and the transceiver state determine whether the command is processed.

points.reached by: the transceiver ==> bus_access arrow carrying rtx_engine.cs_ctrl
points.reason: The bus-access block only reads back cs_ctrl in a response field and does not independently modify or block chip-select generation.

points.reached by: the transceiver --> chip_select arrow carrying rtx_engine.cs_ctrl
points.reason: The stored selection indexes which chip-select output is asserted, so changing or clearing cs_ctrl can select the wrong target or prevent selection.

points.reached by: holding block
points.reason: The registered irq_o value is computed from software-controlled interrupt enables and FIFO or engine status, so those inputs can falsify or suppress the interrupt.

points.reached by: the bus_access ==> irq_generator arrow carrying ctrl.enable and the interrupt-enable fields
points.reason: Unchecked bus writes change the interrupt-enable fields and operational enable, allowing irq_o to be suppressed or asserted under the wrong condition.

points.reached by: the rx_fifo_inst ==> irq_generator arrow carrying rx_fifo.avail
points.reason: Under the black-box rule, the receive FIFO availability output can change the interrupt condition and can prevent a receive-service interrupt from being generated.

points.reached by: the tx_fifo_inst ==> irq_generator arrow carrying tx_fifo.avail and tx_fifo.half
points.reason: Under the black-box rule, transmit FIFO status outputs affect irq_o and can cause missing or incorrect service interrupts.

points.reached by: the transceiver ==> rtx_engine.busy arrow carrying rtx_engine.state
points.reason: The derived busy state participates in the idle interrupt condition, so a faulty or blocked state can suppress or falsely produce irq_o.

points.reached by: the transceiver ==> rtx_engine.busy arrow
points.reason: The transceiver state controls busy, which is used in the idle interrupt expression; stalled or incorrect sequencing can therefore alter interrupt signaling.
